scenes.title: LAST_VALUE()
scenes.narration: LAST_VALUE returns the last value in the window frame, but its default frame hides a surprising gotcha you must understand.

scenes.title: How LAST_VALUE() Works
bullets: Returns the last row's value in the current frame
Order is set by the ORDER BY inside OVER
The frame — not the whole partition — defines 'last'
The default frame ends at the current row, not the partition end
scenes.narration: LAST_VALUE returns the value from the last row in the window frame, ordered by your ORDER BY. The subtle point is that last means the last row of the frame, not the last row of the whole partition. And by default the frame ends at the current row, which is the root of the common confusion around this function.

scenes.title: The Default Frame Gotcha

left.title: Default Frame (Wrong Result)
points: RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
Frame ends at the current row
LAST_VALUE returns the current row's value
Looks broken — it just echoes each row

right.title: Explicit Frame (Correct Result)
points: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
LAST_VALUE returns the true last row
Gives the group's final value as intended

scenes.narration: With the default frame, RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, the frame stops at the current row, so LAST_VALUE just returns each row's own value and appears broken. To get the true last value you must widen the frame explicitly to ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING, which spans the whole partition. Only then does LAST_VALUE return the genuine final row of the group.

scenes.title: Getting the Real Last Value
scenes.code:
SELECT
  department,
  employee_name,
  salary,
  LAST_VALUE(employee_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY department
    ORDER BY salary DESC
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  ) AS lowest_earner
FROM employees;
scenes.narration: Here we partition by department and order by salary descending, so the lowest-paid employee sits last. To reach that row we spell out the frame as ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING, forcing the frame to cover the entire partition. LAST_VALUE of employee_name now correctly returns the lowest earner on every row. Without that explicit frame it would wrongly return each row's own name.

scenes.text: Always add ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING with LAST_VALUE() — or flip your ORDER BY and use FIRST_VALUE() instead.
scenes.narration: Remember to widen the frame with LAST_VALUE, or simply reverse your ORDER BY and use FIRST_VALUE, which avoids the trap entirely.
